title: The unit circle
keyIdea: On the unit circle (radius 1, centre at the origin), the point reached by turning θ anticlockwise from the positive x-axis has coordinates (cos θ, sin θ). This defines sine and cosine for every angle, and the quadrant decides their signs.

kid: Draw a circle with radius 1 and its centre at (0, 0). Start a point at (1, 0) and turn it round the circle the opposite way to a clock's hands. Call the angle it turns θ.
Read the point's place. How far across it is, x, is called cos θ. How far up it is, y, is called sin θ.
On the left side of the circle, x is less than zero, so cos θ is too. Below the middle line, y is less than zero, so sin θ is too.
At 150°, the point is up and to the left. So cos 150° is negative and sin 150° is positive.
adult: Take the circle x² + y² = 1. Turn a radius anticlockwise from the positive x-axis through θ. The end point is defined to be (cos θ, sin θ). For an acute angle this matches SOH CAH TOA: the radius is a hypotenuse of length 1, so the adjacent side is x and the opposite side is y.

The definition works for any angle: 150°, 210°, negative angles (turned clockwise) and angles over 360°. Angles that differ by a full turn, 360° or 2π radians, land on the same point, so sine and cosine repeat.

The quadrant gives the sign. Cosine is positive in quadrants I and IV, right of the y-axis. Sine is positive in I and II, above the x-axis. The size comes from the reference angle, the acute angle to the x-axis. So cos 150° = −cos 30° = −√3/2 and sin 210° = −sin 30° = −1/2.

Every point is 1 from the centre, so cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 for all θ. Common mistakes: swapping the coordinates (cos is x, not y), using the reference angle's signs in every quadrant, turning clockwise for a positive angle, and thinking sine and cosine stop at 90°.

familyTip: Hold a pencil flat on a paper plate, from the centre to the right edge. Turn it anticlockwise to about 150° and ask: is the tip left or right of centre, above or below? That gives the signs of cos 150° and sin 150° before any calculator.

practice.prompt: On the unit circle, what are the coordinates of the point at angle θ?
practice.hint: The radius is a hypotenuse of length 1. Which side is adjacent to θ: across or up?
practice.explain: The across distance is adjacent ÷ 1 = cos θ, and the height is opposite ÷ 1 = sin θ. So the point is (cos θ, sin θ).

practice.prompt: An angle of {a}° is in quadrant II. What is its reference angle, in degrees?
practice.hint: In quadrant II, measure the gap between the radius and the negative x-axis, at 180°.
practice.explain: {a}° is {=180-a}° short of 180°, so the reference angle is {=180-a}°. The point is at the same height as the point at {=180-a}°.

practice.prompt: Turning clockwise by {a}° gives the angle −{a}°. Which angle between 0° and 360° lands on the same point?
practice.hint: A full turn is 360°. Going back {a}° from a full turn ends in the same place.
practice.explain: Clockwise {a}° ends where anticlockwise 360° − {a}° = {=360-a}° does, so both angles have the same sine and cosine.

practice.prompt: Which is true for an angle in quadrant III, between 180° and 270°?
practice.hint: Quadrant III is bottom left. Is x positive or negative there? And y?
practice.explain: Bottom left means left of the y-axis (x < 0) and below the x-axis (y < 0), so both cos θ and sin θ are negative.

practice.hint: Find the reference angle, then ask whether the point is left or right of the y-axis.
practice.explain: The reference angle is 30° and the point is left of the y-axis, so cos 150° = −cos 30° = −√3/2 ≈ −0.866. −1/2 would be cos 120°.

pool.prompt: The point on the unit circle at 210° is (−√3/2, −1/2). What are sin 210° and cos 210°?
pool.hint: The first coordinate is cos θ and the second is sin θ.
pool.explain: x = cos 210° = −√3/2 and y = sin 210° = −1/2. Both are negative because 210° is in quadrant III.

pool.prompt: Why is cos θ negative for angles in the second quadrant?
choices: Points there are left of the y-axis, so their x-coordinate is negative
Angles bigger than 90° always have a negative cosine
Sine and cosine swap signs every 90°
pool.hint: cos θ is one of the point's coordinates. Which one, and where is the point?
pool.explain: cos θ is the x-coordinate, and every point in quadrant II is left of the y-axis. Size alone is not the reason: cos 300° = 1/2 is positive.

pool.prompt: An angle of {a}° is in quadrant III. What is its reference angle, in degrees?
pool.hint: In quadrant III, measure past the negative x-axis, at 180°.
pool.explain: {a}° − 180° = {=a-180}°, so the reference angle is {=a-180}°. Sine and cosine are both negative there.

pool.prompt: Which angle between 0° and 360° lands on the same point of the unit circle as {=a+360*k}°?
pool.hint: Take off full turns of 360° until the angle is less than 360°.

pool.prompt: A point on the unit circle is at (0.6, −0.8). Which statement is true?
choices: cos θ = 0.6 and sin θ = −0.8, so θ is in quadrant IV
cos θ = −0.8 and sin θ = 0.6, so θ is in quadrant II
cos θ = 0.6 and sin θ = −0.8, so θ is in quadrant II
pool.hint: x is cos θ and y is sin θ. Right of the y-axis and below the x-axis is which quadrant?
pool.explain: x = 0.6 = cos θ and y = −0.8 = sin θ. Right and below is quadrant IV. Check: 0.6² + 0.8² = 0.36 + 0.64 = 1.

pool.prompt: In a right triangle with hypotenuse 1, which length is the side adjacent to the acute angle θ?
pool.hint: cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, and the hypotenuse is 1.
pool.explain: Adjacent ÷ 1 = cos θ, so the adjacent side has length cos θ. That is why the unit circle's x-coordinate is cos θ.

pool.hint: A negative angle turns clockwise. Where does a quarter turn clockwise from (1, 0) end?
pool.explain: Clockwise 90° ends at (0, −1), the same point as 270°, so sin(−90°) = −1 and cos(−90°) = 0.

pool.prompt: Which angle has the same sine as 40°?
pool.hint: Sine is the height. Which other point on the circle is at the same height as 40°?
pool.explain: 180° − 40° = 140° is the mirror image across the y-axis, at the same height. 220° and 320° are below the x-axis, so their sines are negative.

pool.prompt: A point on the unit circle in quadrant I has cos θ = 0.28. What is sin θ?
pool.hint: Every point is 1 from the centre, so cos²θ + sin²θ = 1.
pool.explain: sin²θ = 1 − 0.28² = 1 − 0.0784 = 0.9216, so sin θ = 0.96 (positive in quadrant I). 0.72 comes from 1 − 0.28, which forgets the squares.

visual.caption: Legs 8 and 6, hypotenuse 10: cos = 0.8, sin = 0.6. Scale the hypotenuse to 1 and the legs are the unit-circle point (0.8, 0.6).

lab.caption: Flagship lab: turn a point round the unit circle. Its x is cos θ, its y is sin θ, and the graph draws both as you go.
